subject: Budget fit and economic checklist for LumaTech inference pilot
messages:
From: Emma Harper <emma@lumatech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Budget fit & next steps for LumaTech inference pilot

Thanks for the call earlier today. Quick note to capture our immediate constraints so we don’t lose momentum.

Key pain points we reiterated on the call:
- Token cost variability is the main blocker for forecasting monthly spend. We have a high-variance request size distribution (short prompts + occasional long context loads).
- Peak latency matters for user-facing flows (target p95 < 350ms).
- We are sensitive to vendor-hosted data policies — audit logs and retention windows are required for procurement.

Budget situation:
- FY27 budget for experimentation: ~$150k total (pilot + integration). Anything that materially exceeds that needs exec sign-off.
- For production rollout we expect a separate capital ask in Q3 conditional on pilot outcomes.

Next asks from our side:
1) Can you provide a concise TCO snapshot for a 3-week pilot sized at 4 concurrent sessions, ~200M tokens/mo, with and without prefix caching?
2) Short checklist of procurement artifacts (SOC2, retention SLA, sample DPA clauses).
3) A one-pager that frames ROI levers (batching, KV caching, quantization) with expected % token-cost reduction ranges.

Cc’ing our procurement alias so they see the requests.

– Emma
Emma Harper
Head of Product Ops, LumaTech
emma@lumatech.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Emma Harper <emma@lumatech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Budget fit and economic checklist for LumaTech inference pilot

Emma — appreciate the clear summary, and great meeting earlier. Below is our rapid recap plus the deliverables we committed to. I’ll keep this focused so your procurement and finance teams can act quickly.

Recap of pain + goals
- Unpredictable token spend driven by bursty long-context calls. Goal: keep pilot unit cost under $0.0009/token (target blended) and p95 latency < 350ms for user flows.
- Require audit logs & retention policy visibility for procurement.

Proposed 3-week pilot (recommended sizing)
- Traffic profile: 4 concurrent sessions, average request 120 tokens, 10% long-context (>2k tokens) on peak day.
- Infra: Hosted Redwood API (dedicated burst pool) to simplify onboarding and reduce ops overhead. Can transition to Dedicated if you want isolation.

TCO snapshot (high-level ranges — final numbers in attached spreadsheet)
- Baseline (no caching, conservative batching): ~$7k–$9k for 3 weeks (est. 200M tokens).
- With prefix/KV caching + efficient batching: ~$4.5k–$6k for 3 weeks (30–45% token-cost reduction in our model).
- With 8-bit quantized variant on dedicated capacity (if latency/SLO hold): additional ~10–20% unit-cost reduction vs. hosted on large runs.

Primary ROI levers we’ll show in the one-pager
- Batching: smooths per-token latency tradeoff vs throughput; expected 8–25% cost improvement depending on concurrency.
- KV/prefix caching: immediate wins for repeated context patterns (your call logs example).
- Model variant & quantization: best for sustained high-throughput workloads.

Deliverables (we will send these by EOD Monday):
1) redwood-pilot-econ-checklist.xlsx — line-item TCO for pilot variants (attached).
2) One-pager: ROI levers and expected % improvements.
3) Procurement packet: SOC2 summary, retention controls, DPA excerpt.
4) A short proposed SOW + timeline for a 3-week pilot and acceptance criteria.

Suggested next steps / timeline
- Monday: We share attachments and a short internal decision checklist for you.
- Tue/Wed: 30-min alignment call with finance/procurement to confirm budget and signature authority.
- Goal: kickoff pilot the week of Jan 4 (gives your team two weeks to route procurement).

Open questions for you (so we can tailor the spreadsheet):
- Do you have a preferred accounting (capex vs. opex) treatment for pilot invoices?
- Any hard latency SLOs beyond the p95 < 350ms target?

If you prefer, Monica (cc) can run a short technical baseline to capture a “cost at 95th percentile” row for the spreadsheet.

Thanks — will get the files over Monday.

— Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
